verdict.rationale: The product is published as a GitHub repository whose README points to source directories, scripts, and unit tests, so the source appears to be publicly readable. However, nothing in the evidence names a license or shows that it is an open-source one, and the open-license half of the story is the key part. Missing for 10: any stated license (e.g., MIT/Apache/GPL), confirmation that the license is OSI-approved or otherwise open, and independent corroboration of the repo's openness.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
